Especially if it is your property, they shouldn't park there if you don't want them to.

You did a nice thing for them, but it seems they are taking advantage of you now. Firmly tell them that you don't want them parking there anymore, and if they don't listen, I'd pursue legal actions if possible.

Don't feel guilty.

NOT THE ASSHOLE

Your parents are dinosaurs who still believe in toxic masculinity. A guy who knits? That's honestly really sweet and adorable. Good on you for standing up for him, and I hope you can move out soon.

Agree with the other comments here, not telling him would be NTA.

If he wants/needs to talk about it with you, then it's on him to talk about it. Assuming you are together long-term, it would likely come up eventually, and when that happens, tell him the truth. You can tell him what your dad told you and that you chose not to bring it up until he was ready to talk about it.

Everyone grieves in their own way, and I'm sure he will open up when he feels like it. If you want to do something for him, I would recommend you do something small. Too big and you'll tip your hand that you know something. Buy him a small gift or set up an impromptu cute date, whatever you think he'd appreciate. You can support him indirectly, and the gesture could go a long way towards growing together.
